Leading indicators point to higher US inflation.

The ISM Services Prices Paid Index rose +2.3 points in August, to 72.6, its highest since July 2022.

Since February, the index has risen +9.6 points, its largest 6-month increase since May 2025.

Historically, this metric has led CPI inflation and core PCE inflation by ~6 months.

If the historical relationship holds, the current reading suggests CPI could rise to as high as 6.0% in the coming months, from 3.4% in July.

At the same time, this implies core PCE could increase above 4.0%, from July’s reported 3.3%.

Inflation pressures are intensifying in the US.

BREAKING: Copper prices on the LME have surged to a record $14,533 per ton, now up +47% over the last 12 months.

The surge comes amid a supply shortage with rising demand from data centers, renewable energy, and power grids.

Furthermore, expectations that President Trump will expand tariffs to refined copper imports have pushed US Comex prices above global prices.

This is encouraging traders to ship hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US this year to profit from the price difference.

Now, global stockpiles are increasingly concentrated in the US, draining LME inventories to critically low levels and leaving less copper readily available to buyers elsewhere.

Copper's supply crunch is accelerating.
This is constructive for $ETH

Retail appetite for chip stocks has eased:

Retail purchases of the semiconductor ETFs, $SOXL, $SOXX, and $SMH, are now 1 standard deviation below their 1-year average.

At one point in mid-June, purchases fell to 2 standard deviations below this historical norm.

This metric is now well below the peak seen in November 2025 and March 2026, at 3 standard deviations above its 1-year average.

Similarly, retail purchases of individual semiconductor stocks fell to more than 2 standard deviations below their historical norm last month.

Retail investors are buying significantly fewer semiconductor stocks and ETFs than they were before the sector sell-off in June through July.

The AI trade remains highly fluid.

US homebuyers are walking away from deals at the highest rate in years:

14.0% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in July, the highest rate since November 2023.

The national cancellation rate has held between 13.0% and 14.0% over the last 4 years, well above the lower rates typical of the seller's market from 2020 to 2022.

Atlanta posted the highest cancellation rate last month, at 19.8%, followed by Houston at 19.6%, San Antonio at 18.7%, and Las Vegas at 18.6%.

This comes as sellers outnumber buyers by ~51%, near the highest percentage on record, giving buyers more options and making them more willing to walk away over inspection issues, low appraisals, or rejected concessions.

At the same time, high home prices and elevated mortgage rates are leaving buyers with less financial room, making unexpected costs or concerns about taking on large monthly payments more likely to derail deals.

The housing market is under historic pressure.

Non-asset owners are very worried about inflation.

The 3-month moving average of 1-year inflation expectations among US consumers with no stock holdings hit ~5.0% in August, near the highest level this year.

This is significantly above the ~3.0% recorded in late 2024.

Meanwhile, the 3-month moving average of inflation expectations among US consumers with the largest stock holdings remained below 4.0% last month.

Readings for both groups were roughly in-line with levels seen in late-2022, following the recovery from the energy crisis.

Asset owners are the only winners in this economy.

BREAKING: US data center construction spending surged +57% YoY in July, to a record annualized rate of $75 billion.

This follows a +46% YoY increase in June and marks the largest YoY increase since mid-2025.

Since the start of 2021, US data center construction spending has soared +$66 billion, or +717%.

Since the end of 2023 alone, data center construction has risen +$51 billion.

Over the same period, all other private construction spending, including houses, shopping centers, and offices, has declined -$120 billion.

The AI investment wave is accelerating.
Simply an extraordinary tribute to the Twin Towers

China just had its best earnings season in years:

Profits at Chinese companies listed in mainland China surged +25.7% YoY in Q2 2026, the highest growth rate since Q2 2021.

This also marks the 2nd consecutive quarter of positive earnings growth following a double-digit decline in Q4 2025.

The surge was driven by AI-linked companies, with earnings up +42% on Shenzhen’s growth-focused ChiNext market and +370% on Shanghai’s technology-focused STAR Market, significantly outpacing the broader market.

Despite this outstanding performance, the CSI 300 Index has fallen -9% so far this quarter, while the tech-heavy STAR 50 Index has dropped -29%.

China is experiencing a historic earnings boom due to AI.
